newsitem.title: USA: Schwab has 830,000 on-line account holders.
newsitem.headline: Schwab has 830,000 on-line account holders.

text.p: Charles Schwab Corp vice president Karen Askey said the brokerage house had a total of 830,000 active on-line account holders at the end of May, representing more than $56 billion in assets.
Askey told reporters after a presentation here that on-line trades accounted for 35 percent of the brokerage's total transactions at the end of May.

Askey, who heads Schwab's electronic brokerage marketing, said the company counts as an active on-line investor any person who has logged onto the company's system using their computer in the last year. This includes people who have used Schwab's dialup software as well as Internet access.

The executive declined to break down the number of Internet-based accounts versus conventional on-line accounts, but she said the statistics do not double count people who use both systems, adding that electronic trade activity is now about 50-50 conventional on-line vs Internet.
Recent electronic trading growth has been in Internet trading, which went live to the general public last July.

The 830,000 active online brokerage accounts is up nearly 25 percent in a two month period from the 750,000 active accounts, representing $50 billion in assets, which it reported at the end of March. But the 35 percent of total trading volume attributable to electronic services was only up two percentage points at the end of May from two months earlier.

Schwab's basic charge for electronic trades is $29.95, about a $10 premium over the base rates of other discount online brokers, and Askey said Schwab was seeking to differentiate its service with stronger support at this level.
Brokerages offering services over the Internet have been growing their online volumes dramatically, although they typically use different measures for reporting trade levels.

E*TRADE Group, Inc., based in Palo Alto, Calif., also provides Internet and online trading and reported a rise in its overall customer base in its most recent quarter, but did not break down electronic versus more conventional trade.

E*TRADE reported its active customers had grown by 29 percent in its March quarter to 145,000 accounts with assets of more than $4.1 billion, a 25 percent rise from $3.3 billion at the end of December 1996, for example.
Askey said the electronic trading activity has demonstrated the power and cost savings online transactions can generate.

Schwab has handled over 10,000 simultaneous transactions, she said, which is more than double the number of registered representatives Schwab has and therefore at least twice as many as the company's staff could handle at maximum work levels.
The company has handled electronic trades from customers in more than 76 countries, she added.
"The Web has allowed Schwab to experience tremendous growth in the online accounts," she said.
Askey declined to discus the company's investment in electronic trading specifically, but said it spends $300 million a year on technology, including databases.
